Notes: Co-elevated BCL2L1 (TPM=31), MCL1 (TPM=134) in PM154 suggests navitoclax may add benefit by dual BCL2/BCL-XL inhibition; MCL1 selective inhibitors (S64315, AZD5991) also of interest.
N-Myc/Aurora-A complex disruption (Beltran 2019) is the molecular rationale; combinations with venetoclax or platinum may be additive.
If AURKB enrichment is the dominant signal (as seen in MIBC), barasertib may be more on-target than alisertib.
Mevrometostat in CRPC enzalutamide-combination trials; CPI-1205 advancing in NHL/solid tumors.

Additional FDA-approved agents: Azacitidine (Vidaza); Decitabine+cedazuridine (Inqovi, oral); CC-486 / oral azacitidine (Onureg, AML maintenance)
Notes: Oral options (Inqovi, Onureg) improve outpatient combination feasibility; guadecitabine remains investigational after mixed Phase III results.
Talazoparib has higher PARP-trapping potency; niraparib has CNS penetration; rucaparib has BARD1/CHEK2 spectrum.
Burgess et al. 2019 reported AURKA-high MIBC OS HR=6.10 after NAC; barasertib's AURKB-selectivity matches MIBC's strongest panel signal (AURKB log2FC=+4.08).
TTK is the strongest panel finding after AURKB (log2FC=+3.60 in GSE130598); under active investigation in solid tumors.
PLK1 log2FC=+3.54 in MIBC kinome; volasertib in Phase II AML; onvansertib in Phase II CRC.
CHEK1 log2FC=+2.46 in MIBC; checkpoint inhibition synergizes with WEE1 inhibition.
WEE1 log2FC=−1.12 in MIBC suggests checkpoint bypass; WEE1 inhibition may resensitize.

Pemigatinib and futibatinib have different isoform-selectivity profiles; futibatinib is covalent and active against some resistance mutations. ⚠ Infigratinib (Truseltiq): FDA approval withdrawn 2024 — no longer commercially available.
BAYOU (durvalumab+olaparib) showed mixed results; mUC trials ongoing with combination strategies.

Additional FDA-approved agents: Inavolisib (approved in combination with palbociclib + fulvestrant for PIK3CA-mutated HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer)
Notes: Inavolisib has improved selectivity and lower hyperglycemia versus alpelisib but is indication-specific (breast). ⚠ Copanlisib (Aliqopa): FDA-withdrew the relapsed follicular lymphoma indication in 2024 — no longer approved for B-cell NHL.

Late-stage investigational agents: Disitamab vedotin (HER2-positive bladder also developed; not NECTIN4); EV combinations under investigation
Notes: Currently no other approved anti-NECTIN4 ADC; future bispecific and CAR-T approaches in development.
Multiple approved options with varying biomarker thresholds; combination with EV (per EV-302) currently SOC.
Abemaciclib has best CNS penetration; ribociclib has strongest OS data in HR+ breast.

Additional FDA-approved agents: Sunitinib; Axitinib; Lenvatinib; Cabozantinib (also MET/AXL); Tivozanib
Notes: Cabozantinib (MET/AXL/VEGFR multikinase) has shown particular sRCC activity in CheckMate 9ER and ANTHEM; tivozanib is more VEGFR-selective with lower off-target toxicity.

Late-stage investigational agents: MK-3795; ARO-HIF2 (HIF2α-targeted siRNA); next-gen HIF2 inhibitors in development
Notes: Belzutifan is currently the only approved HIF2α inhibitor; ARO-HIF2 in Phase I.
Limited RCC-specific data; rationale rests on CDKN2A-deleted KIRC subset (~3%).
